enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
518 PM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 517 PM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

 - Widespread chances for showers and thunderstorms through
   Saturday as moisture moves north into the region. Some stronger
   storms could result in flash flooding, damaging winds, and
   large hail. Showers/storms likely limited to Otero/Hudspeth
   Counties Sunday and Monday.

 - Temperatures will be cooling down below normal by Saturday and
   beyond.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1149 AM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

An active pattern setting up across the region as the upper low
that has brought severe weather to AZ has moved onshore into CA
and the southwest flow over the Borderland continues to increase.
Dew points currently up into the 50s for much of the CWA and
instability/shear increasing. CAPE values near AZ border
approaching 1000J/kg and combined with 35-45KTS shear, severe
storms are possible. Also, KLSB observation currently 13013G22KTS
would add to some increased 0-1km low level shear/helicity. Could
see a tornado develop with initial storms which will likely occur
by 20Z. Tornado watch will be out until early evening. Looking
like heavy rain threat with training possibilities over the Gila
region and possibly down into northern Hidalgo, so will leave
Flood Watch as is. Rainfall amounts of 0.5-1.0" with localized
2-3" possible.  

As we go into Fri-Sat, upper low becomes established over AZ and
will be slow to move out. There will be a shift in higher PoPs
toward the RGV for Fri and then eastern areas for Sat. Increasing
mid level flow with a SSE surface wind will continue to keep shear
values high and instability will be there as well, so severe
threat continues. Not sure the tornado threat will be as high as
today though. Again, locally heavy rain will be possible with the
above normal PW's and training threat there. NBM PoPs seemed
reasonable and higher than the operational GFS, but more in line
with the GEFS which puts high chance to low likely PoPs to the
RGV. May need to put a Flood Watch out later for at least 
Hudspeth and Otero counties.

Sunday is the questionable day. Model trend is to slow down the
timing of the upper low moving out. The trough axis will at least
remain off to our west through 00Z Mon and with that, will keep
some PoPs going east of the Rio Grande Valley. Best moisture will
be moving out, but still some convective potential for moderate
rainfall and a marginal severe threat over far eastern zones.  

Still keeping a slight trough through the east even into Monday
with some rain chances continuing and even a continued low severe
threat. Tuesday looks drier with ridge passing overhead but rain
chances return Wed. Temperatures by Sunday will be getting closer
to normal and remain there.  

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 517 PM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Lower VFR conditions through the period with SCT080 BKN150 BKN250.
Isolated OVC050 3-5SM TSRA west of Deming, but slowly spreading
east to the Rio Grande Valley this evening. Large hail and wind
gusts to 45 knots possible with some of these storms. South to
southeast winds 8-12G20 knots becoming variable AOB 7 knots after
03Z. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1149 AM MDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Fire threat remains low will another round of widespread showers
and thunderstorms through the weekend. Temperatures will be
cooling to near normal with RH's remaining above 30%. Some
thunderstorms will be severe over the coming days and wind gusts
over 50mph will be possible with the strongest storms.
